newsitem.title: USA: U.S. average retail beef prices steady in month.
newsitem.headline: U.S. average retail beef prices steady in month.

text.p: Average retail beef prices showed little change during the past month, the National Cattlemen's Beef Association (NCBA) said in a report.

The NCBA, summarizing its regular monthly 19-city survey of supermarkets, said the average price of six cuts of beef on September 12 was $2.97 per lb, compared with $2.95 on August 8 and and $3.02 a year ago. It said the six-cut average has varied little in the last six months and remained near the lowest levels since six-cut surveys began in 1991.
Beef production decreased recently and wholesale prices have risen, the NCBA said.
However, retailers continued to feature ground beef as well as steaks and other cuts at special low prices, the NCBA said. The result has been numerous beef bargains for consumers, it said.
The NCBA six-cut average on September 12 was up from a month earlier in 12 cities and down in seven, the group said.

The 19-city averages for the six cuts on September 12 were as follows: regular ground beef, $1.43 per lb; lean ground beef, $1.86; boneless round steak, $2.88; boneless top sirloin steak, $3.68; T-bone steak, $5.62; and boneless chuck roll roast $2.35.
